notes: PARALLEL APPROVAL MECHANISMS (2026-07-28 N17 pilot Task 1 finding, directly re-verified): ActionContracts is the canonical lifecycle authority, but 4 coexisting, independently-reachable approve/reject mechanisms are live on main, not 1: (1) ActionContract/ActionGateway itself — durable, `ActionContractRepository` (core/action_contract_repository.py), TTL `CONTRACT_PENDING_TTL_SECONDS=24h` (core/action_contract_repository.py:84); (2) EventBus's `PendingActionsStore` — pure in-memory dict, no durable backing, class at event_bus.py:28, TTL `PENDING_TTL_MINUTES=30` (event_bus.py:26); populated unconditionally from `_queue_approval_detailed_impl` even when the Gateway already approved, i.e. it runs alongside (1), not instead of it; (3) app.py's router-level `_pending_approvals` dict — a second, separate pure in-memory store (app.py:170, lock at app.py:174), TTL `_PENDING_APPROVAL_TTL=600s` (app.py:228), drives the text-based כן/לא confirmation flow; (4) the TMA dashboard's Airtable-backed Approvals-table flow (tma_api.py, routes registered app.py:427) with its own TTL `_TMA_APPROVAL_TTL_SECONDS=24h` (tma_api.py:2162), though execution is delegated back to ActionGateway. A symptom like 'repeated approval returns the wrong message' can originate in any of these four, not only in ActionContract state. `core/approvals_projection.py`'s own module docstring says it is unwired/dead code; it is not a 5th live mechanism. `session_store.py`'s `pending_lead_preview` is a separate lead-classification confirmation flow, not an approval mechanism — easy to conflate with the four above, but out of this layer's scope.
ActionContracts remains the sole source of truth for approval lifecycle.
Legacy IDs may resolve an existing unambiguous canonical contract but may never create or infer one.
Approval state, presentation state, and execution evidence are distinct.

PR #471: Telegram approve/reject callback_data now carries an optional trailing contract_id (_approval_callback_data(), app.py:1128); when present and FEATURE_ACTION_GATEWAY is on, the callback resolves the exact ActionContract via lifecycle_result() before falling back to fingerprint matching.

PR #471 (BUG-144): the reject callback now resolves and closes the canonical ActionContract (reject_with_lifecycle_result()) before reporting cancellation to the user, not just the legacy EventBus item.

ApprovalLifecycleResult (core/action_gateway.py) is the single-speaker, user-safe projection of one ActionContract lifecycle; approve_with_lifecycle_result()/reject_with_lifecycle_result() are the canonical entry points that produce it. This is layered on top of, not a replacement for, ActionContracts as lifecycle authority.

PR #479/#480 (merged, N17 re-verification): changed only the rendered wording of build_approval_lifecycle_result() and _describe_tool_call() (rejected-state phrasing normalized to 'בוטלה', task-creation gets dedicated business wording, raw Airtable table names no longer leak into any approval message) — no lifecycle, callback-resolution, or authority change.
